title: Open restriction and finite-cover preservation for exceptional comparisons
statement:
Use the finite-field datum, finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$ and the actual ordinary-etale and transported constructible operations of [sk-def-sf-operations]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes; the schemes need not be separated over $k$. For open immersions $u:W\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $f':W\to V$ with $fu=vf'$, there is a canonical isomorphism $u^*Rf^!K\cong Rf'^!v^*K$, initially defined by the ordinary-etale adjoints and transported at finite constructible coefficients. For an additional open $w:Z'\hookrightarrow Z$, restriction along $u\times w$ carries the Ku_!–counit transpose $\alpha_{f,\mathrm{id}_Z}(K,Q)$ of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] to $\alpha_{f',\mathrm{id}_{Z'}}(v^*K,w^*Q)$ under these isomorphisms. No invertibility of either comparison is assumed or concluded.
Moreover, if the restrictions of $Rf^!K$ to a finite open cover of $X$ have bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, then $Rf^!K$ does also. An interval containing the finitely many local cohomology intervals, and an interval containing the finitely many local Tor intervals, are global bounds. The same assertion holds with uniform finite-reduction bounds for the normalized integral construction of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi).
